title: Canonical EffectGate/EffectJournal authority is named, but exact current executable implementation identity is not yet bound to the Frankenstein 2.0 interlock
claim_under_review: The current Frankenstein 2.0 executor interlock can now be integrated directly with the canonical EffectGate/EffectJournal implementation without another authority-resolution gate.

observations.fact: Current-facing EntityOS manifest names EffectGate+EffectJournal as the sole real-effect authority but does not bind an exact current executable implementation path/blob/API identity.
Current architecture preserves the abstract candidate -> EffectGate + EffectJournal -> reality boundary while classifying ClayVerse/Frank as historical donor/provenance unless explicitly re-admitted.

Compatibility/donor EffectGate source allocates effect authority through EffectJournal before side effects, but it is under a ClayVerse compatibility path and current architecture does not by itself re-admit that path as the executable EntityOS implementation.
Compatibility/donor EffectJournal allocates effect_id internally in begin() and persists PENDING before action; this identity order is materially different from a caller-prebound effect_id contract.
The F2 interlock correctly refuses to mint policy and requires ExternalGateEvidence from the canonical authority, but its production authority_ref/decision_id source is intentionally unresolved.
Repository CI proves policy-neutral external-gate -> executor interlock behavior only; canonical EffectGate integration and EffectJournal integration remain zero credit.

reason: Authority semantics are clear, but an abstract authority name is not an executable implementation identity. Binding F2 directly to a compatibility/donor path without an explicit current admission would risk silently promoting historical implementation provenance; letting F2 mint its own policy/journal would create a forbidden second authority.

identity_order_constraint.observed_f2_requirement: A PREPARED call/effect identity must exist before executor dispatch and external ALLOW must match that exact call.
identity_order_constraint.observed_donor_journal_order: EffectJournal.begin() allocates effect_id transactionally and persists PENDING before the side effect.
identity_order_constraint.safe_convergence_rule: The canonical authority must remain the source of authoritative effect identity. Either the current canonical implementation explicitly admits a predeclared effect_id under transactional exact-call validation, or the integration API must let canonical begin/admission allocate the effect_id and return an authority-bound pre-dispatch envelope before executor dispatch. F2 must not invent a second effect identity namespace that canonical state later merely accepts post hoc.

preferred_successor_contract: 1. Resolve one exact current effect-authority implementation identity: repository + path/module + source blob/commit + state/journal schema identity + API/adapter version.
2. If a historical compatibility path is intentionally re-admitted, record that admission explicitly under current EntityOS authority instead of inferring it from source existence.
3. Accept a result-free NativeChildBinding/call identity before dispatch; do not require WP104/WP105 post-result objects to construct the authority request.
4. Canonical authority validates capability, generation, permission/replay fences and allocates or transactionally admits the authoritative effect_id before any executor call.
5. Return ExternalGateEvidence bound to exact effect_id + binding_id + invocation_id + tool_use_id + delegation_id + child identity and an exact authority/source identity.
6. Only exact ALLOW may reach the executor. DENY/REQUIRE_CONFIRMATION/DEGRADE/UNKNOWN and authority-resolution failure call the executor zero times.
7. Persist DISPATCH_STARTED/PENDING before an effect may occur; exceptions after possible dispatch remain UNKNOWN and forbid blind replay until reconciliation/world verification.
8. POST execution receipt must echo exact effect/call identity. Executor success is not world verification and cannot mint WP105 completion by itself.
9. No second F2 truth database, policy engine, EffectGate, EffectJournal, or hidden recovery ledger is introduced.
counterhypothesis: the artefact/clayverse EffectGate+EffectJournal may already be the intentionally current executable compatibility implementation despite the historical compatibility namespace.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator: Find or create a current-authority binding record that explicitly names the executable EffectGate/EffectJournal implementation path/blob/API/schema identity. If the compatibility ClayVerse path is the admitted implementation, bind that fact explicitly; if not, identify the actual current implementation. Only then run the deterministic canonical-authority -> F2 interlock integration matrix.
do_not_do: Do not copy EffectGate policy into Frankenstein 2.0.
Do not treat source-file existence or architecture prose as runtime integration evidence.
Do not let a caller-authored authority_ref or effect_id self-grant canonical effect authority.
Do not overwrite the active F2-WP-105 implementation claim from this review-only organ.
Do not perform a real external effect, provider call, VPS test, paid action or unusual experiment for this discriminator.
next_exact_action_for_active_mutation_au: Resolve and bind the exact current canonical EffectGate/EffectJournal executable implementation identity, then adapt the result-free pre-dispatch call identity so the canonical authority produces or transactionally admits the authoritative effect_id before F2 dispatch; run the existing DENY/UNKNOWN/no-replay matrix plus restart reconciliation without weakening WP104/WP105 post-result contracts.
